chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Looking towards the Ka'bah is worship, and looking towards the parents is worship, and looking at the Imam is worship.
And he said: 'The one who looks towards the Ka'bah, one good deed is written for him and ten sins are deleted from him'.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for looking at the Ka'bah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elevates the physical act of 'looking' (nazar) into a spiritual discipline, linking the veneration of the Ka'bah, parents, and the Imam as parallel forms of worship. Historically, this reflects the Shia emphasis on the Imam as the living proof of God, where gazing upon him carries similar merit to gazing upon the House of God. The specific reward of one good deed for ten sins erased highlights the disproportionate grace associated with these sacred gazes.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The looking towards the Kabah is (an act of) worship, and the looking towards the parents is (an act of) worship, and the looking at the Imam<sup>asws</sup> is (an act of) worship’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who looks towards the Kabah, one good deed is written for him and ten sins are deleted from him’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
looking at al-Ka’bah is an act of worship; looking at parents is an act of worship; and looking at the Imam is an act of worship.
For one’s looking at al- Ka’bah, one good deed is written for him and ten of his bad deeds are deleted.”
